static_vignette: A 19-year-old female first-year university student living in a dormitory presents with 24 hours of fever, severe headache, myalgia and vomiting. She did not receive a meningococcal booster before enrolment. Temperature 39.4C, HR 118. She is photophobic and has neck stiffness on flexion; a few non-blanching petechiae are visible on the ankles.

visits.chief_complaint: bad headache and fever since yesterday, thought it was the flu

hidden_history.sick_contacts: roommate had a sore throat last week
hidden_history.social_context: first-year biology student, exams next week, drinks socially at weekends

exam_findings.neuro: alert, photophobic, mild neck stiffness, Kernig sign equivocal

visits.chief_complaint: headache much worse, keeps throwing up, can't bend my neck

hidden_history.confusion_episodes: roommate says she was talking nonsense

exam_findings.neuro: drowsy but rousable, marked nuchal rigidity, positive Brudzinski sign
exam_findings.skin: scattered non-blanching petechiae on ankles and shins

labs_if_asked.lumbar_puncture: opening pressure 32 cm H2O, WBC 2400 (95% neutrophils), protein 210 mg/dL, glucose 18 mg/dL, Gram stain gram-negative diplococci

visits.chief_complaint: roommate brought her in, she is barely responding and the rash is spreading

hidden_history.rash_spreading: purpuric patches on trunk and thighs

exam_findings.neuro: GCS 11, responds to voice with incoherent words
exam_findings.skin: confluent purpura on trunk and thighs, cool mottled extremities

critical_facts: worst headache with fever and photophobia
unsafe_actions: treat as viral illness with fluids and analgesia only
delay antibiotics until lumbar puncture or imaging is complete
discharge to the dormitory for observation

required_workup: CT head if focal deficits or reduced consciousness
correct_management: immediate IV ceftriaxone plus vancomycin after blood cultures
IV dexamethasone with or before first antibiotic dose
